Pat Newell, taking over Jack Brown's cloak, proved a worthy successor on the hard grind from Crawley to Handcross, and in gaining two places brought us within sight of all but T.V.H. who had widened their lead,through a grand run by Bert Ingles, to 2½ minutes over the second club, Woodford.
Walker, John Moore and Pat Newell to decide the issue, with Eric Gebbett, Malcolm Robinson and Alan Black forming the spearhead of the second bunch.

Good times were recorded by Baulch, Bhatia, Davies and Newell. These two races,followed by our own 5¾ miles road race and 3 miles yacht handicap, preceded the London to Brighton Relay for Southern clubs on October 11th and we had every reason to think we were set for a place - in actual fact we had…

On a hot summer evening, and on a bone hard track Pat Newell the defending champion, and fifteen challengers faced the starter. After only one lap 'Glimpy' Jones and Dereck Crooks were a good twenty yards up on Pat and going as though they were after an international vest!

Normally our middle-distance men could have split forces but on this occasion we had Newell, Robinson, Dabbs and Radford on holiday, Davies injured and Bhatia a 'flu victim; so it was decided to concentrate our remaining forces on the only major road-relay event we tackle before the "Brighton".
A few weeks later we travelled to West Bromwich for the National, without such stars as Newell (unfit) Bhatia and Moore; both of whom are ineligible for birth reasons.
On the other hand our runners continue to improve, for in the 2 miles Invitation team race Newell (9-18.4), Dabbs (9-23.8) and Robinson (9-30.2) were only 5 points behind the winners, Polytechnic.
In a tactical half-mile, Robinson and Newell were placed second and third in 1:59.9 and 2:00.2 respectively, and in a similarly run 1500 metres Shipley (second claim) was second in 4:6.2.
CENTRE RIGHT: Clive Shippen leads at the water-jump in the "Brockman" steeplechase. BOTTOM LEFT: Kerr (42), Robinson (43), and Newell (41) trail Haith during the "Sword" 2 mls.
Kerr, Newell, Davies, Walker, Black, Dabbs, Linstead, Maclean. How's that for a line up to set a new 3 mile record?

Although the winner finished over a minute ahead of the field, the race was full of interest throughout and many observers were speculating as to the humdinger that would ensue if the absent Kerr and Newell were able to get amongst 'this lot'.

CENTRE LEFT: Linstead, the holder, leads Newell and Black in the Club 10 miles Championship for the "Macher" shield. CENTRE RIGHT: Walker, Black, Sawyer, Thresher and North head the field at 2½ miles in the Club 7 miles 6hampionship for the "Blackstaffe" shield.

On paper we had high hopes of being second to Portsmouth AC but once again we were unable to field a truly representative team and the ten that did start were dogged by misfortune.Those that were unable to appear were Linstead (injury), Thresher (cold), Newell (work) and Roffey (flu).
SURREY: Gerry North, Thresher, Fairclough, Steer, Dabbs, Black. MIDDLESEX: Hart, O'Hara, Kerr, Newell, Dear and Crookes. What a pity that Geoff North, Thorpe, Barrow and Brown qualify for neither!
With Gerry North, Thresher and Barrow not running (besides other possibles like Newell, Reilly, Dance and Kerr) this surely would have produced our fastest "Brighton" team.
Laurie O'Hara and Charlie Dabbs are close behind with 7 and it is interesting to note that the 'old school' of Walker, Dabbs, Newell and Baulch are jointly responsible for 26% of the list.
